description: The judgement half of a landscape, run over scans that already exist. domain-landscape-discovery-v0 does the whole arc — frame, scout, evidence, then relate → fit → attack → map (deterministic assembly) → gate — and its scouting phase is by far its most expensive. When the scans and their evidence check are already sealed (a run that stopped after them, or a landscape being re-judged against changed needs), this standard takes the charter, the landscape-scan records and the landscape-verification as its dispatch payload and runs only the judgement: relate → fit → attack → map (deterministic assembly) → gate. Same seats, same gate, same refusal discipline — an item the evidence check did not verify cannot enter the map here either.

phases.name: relate
phases.intent: Connect the verified items into a typed relation graph, each relation with evidence. Scans and verification arrive as the dispatch payload.

phases.name: fit
phases.intent: Judge each verified item against the needs and competency questions; name the questions nothing covers.

phases.name: attack
phases.intent: Break the landscape: missing items, wrong layers, overclaims, relations that do not hold, questions falsely covered.

phases.name: map
phases.intent: Assemble the layered map from sealed results only. Deterministic: a map is a projection, so assembly is layout rather than judgement — and a model seat here hit the 32k output ceiling trying to emit 64 items in one response.

phases.name: gate
phases.intent: Deterministic guard: only verified, evidenced items survive; relations and fits touching a dropped item go with them; an unresolved blocker marks the map BLOCKED; an empty map is never READY.
